title: Chapter 58: Red Dancing Shoes
html:
Chen Ge’s face was less than a handspan from the mirror, giving him a clearer view than he wanted. Fresh blood soaked the elegant school uniform and molded it to her body. Hair veiled her face, leaving only glimpses of deathly pale skin.

The cold light from his phone warped. His limbs stiffened, and it took all his strength to make his lips form the girl’s name.

“Zhang Ya?”

At the sound of his voice, the girl slowly raised her head. Her black hair parted to reveal a flawless face. Before she could look up fully, mist spread across the glass. She took one step forward and vanished from the reflection.

“Where did she go?”

As he stared at the empty mirror, something stranger happened. In the light of his fallen phone, his shadow slowly rose from the floor and stood behind him.

It was roughly 1.7 meters tall. A sound like dripping blood reached his ears, and color bled into the silhouette until it wore a uniform drenched entirely in red.

Chen Ge did not dare move. Cold raced from his back to the base of his skull. Then the red shadow stepped closer and pressed itself against him.

They stood back to back. His body locked rigid, and no matter how deeply he gasped, he could not draw enough air.

The specter has stuck to my back?

There was a special terror in standing back to back with someone you could not see.

Something cold reached for his fingers. He dared not turn. His numb hand opened, and the phone slipped to the floor. Its light flickered twice, then died.

Surrounded by darkness, Chen Ge felt the cold at his back continue to spread. He could scarcely comprehend what was happening. Two in the morning, inside an abandoned school’s dance studio, facing a full-length mirror, back to back with a Red Specter… I suppose this counts as romance.

Thoughts tumbled through his mind. Whatever held his hand drew more warmth from him with every second. Behind him, the girl’s hair stirred and twined through his own.

What is she planning? I’m supposed to find the red dancing shoes. If I don’t do that before dawn, I’ll fail the mission.

His body refused to move. All he could do was stare into the mirror. At first he missed the vague shapes gathering in its depths. Then they began to sharpen, and his eyes widened.

Wait, aren’t these the girls who are trapped inside the chairs?

Five girls in clean uniforms entered the reflected studio. They looked nothing like the apparitions he had seen, and he realized the mirror was showing him the past.

Laughing among themselves, the five approached the mirrors. Zhang Ya entered soon afterward. Though dressed in the same uniform, she carried herself with a grace the others lacked.

She carried the bag Chen Ge had found in the dressing room—the one that held the five boxes of candy.

Zhang Ya seemed happy. She hurried into the dressing room, and several minutes later all six girls emerged in ballet dresses.

The group’s dynamic had not changed. The five girls clustered together while Zhang Ya trailed behind alone.

Soon after practice began, a female teacher entered holding their Swan Lake certificate. She spoke animatedly, apparently congratulating and encouraging them.

No other students appeared. The six girls had likely come in outside normal school hours for intensive training before the provincial competition.

The teacher left after half an hour. Once they were sure she was gone, five of the girls sprawled on the floor to chat and play with their phones. Zhang Ya alone continued practicing.

One girl pointed at Zhang Ya and said something that made the others laugh. Zhang Ya did not join them, but she seemed untroubled. After a little more practice, she went into the dressing room and returned with the bag of candy.

She offered the boxes to the group. One girl reached for a gift, but another—nearly as tall as Zhang Ya—stopped her. She jabbed an accusing finger at Zhang Ya, then ran into the dressing room and returned with a schoolbag. From it she produced several love letters, all addressed to Zhang Ya.

It was not an argument so much as a one-sided attack. The other girl did all the shouting while Zhang Ya stood silent.

Her gifts rejected, Zhang Ya returned them to the bag and left. Chen Ge thought the scene was over, but the studio door soon opened again. Startled, the five girls scrambled up and pretended to practice.

A blurred male figure entered. He stood about 1.8 meters tall, broad and heavy, with a pronounced slouch.

He addressed the girls, but only two replied. Chen Ge could not tell who the man was.

The girls resumed practicing, and the man went into the office. Later he opened its door and beckoned Zhang Ya over. She appeared neither to know nor trust him. After approaching reluctantly, she stopped at the threshold and refused to enter.

The mirror showed nothing inside the office. Eight seconds later, the reflection darkened and Zhang Ya burst back out. Clutching one arm, the man pursued her with curses pouring from his mouth.

The five girls witnessed everything but remained where they were. Not one moved to help. The man cornered Zhang Ya far from the exit. She screamed, but no one answered. Her classmates pretended not to hear.

The man spat obscenities as he closed in. Behind Zhang Ya, her hands found the edge of the window. Only one escape remained.

Watching the past unfold, Chen Ge remembered the words that had appeared on the black phone when he received the love letter.

Her eyes wide, her cheeks white as ash—the moment she fell from the building, she became the school’s taboo. Red dancing shoes, a blood-dyed uniform; even her name could be spoken only in frightened whispers.

The man peered through the empty window but made no attempt to save Zhang Ya. Instead, he stepped back and joined the five girls, who sat stunned into silence.
